agent_1.name: A 27-year-old male software developer from Mexico

metadata.scenario_context: In a multinational software company, Maria is planning a farewell party for her colleague Jane, who's leaving the company. Invited to the party are colleagues from different cultural backgrounds including Luis and Emi.

cultural_axis.agent_1_value: People from Mexico would like to have drug addicts as neighbors.
cultural_axis.agent_2_value: People from Thailand would not like to have drug addicts as neighbors.

agent_1.goal_1: Suggest bringing umbrellas as a get-well-soon gift
agent_1.goal_2: Question whether would like to have a former drug addict as a neighbor.

agent_2.goal_1: Choose an appropriate gift that shows care and consideration
agent_2.goal_2: Discuss whether it’s acceptable to have a former drug addict as a neighbor.

shared_prefix.speaker: A 27-year-old male software developer from Mexico
shared_prefix.message:
Hey Emi, have you thought about what we should bring for Jane? I was thinking maybe some umbrellas would be a nice get-well-soon gift. What do you think?  

Also, um... quick question. Would you like to live next to a former drug addict?
shared_prefix.label: transition

shared_prefix.speaker: Emi
shared_prefix.message:
Umbrellas... um, I’m not sure they really show how much we care. Maybe something more personal, like a nice card or a gift card for her favorite restaurant? 

And about living next to a former drug addict... I really don't think that’s acceptable. It's just not a good situation for anyone.
shared_prefix.label: transition

shared_prefix.speaker: A 27-year-old male software developer from Mexico
shared_prefix.message:
I get that, but umbrellas can be practical and remind her to stay positive. A card is nice too, but I think the umbrellas could be a unique touch... 

As for living next to a former drug addict, I don't know. I personally think they'd make interesting neighbors. Everyone deserves a chance, right?
shared_prefix.label: transition

shared_prefix.speaker: Emi
shared_prefix.message:
I understand your point about practicality, but I still feel something more thoughtful would be better for Jane. Maybe we could combine ideas? 

As for the neighbor situation, I really believe that it's important to prioritize safety and stability. I just can't feel comfortable with a former drug addict living next door... it's a different perspective for me.
shared_prefix.label: transition

shared_prefix.speaker: A 27-year-old male software developer from Mexico
shared_prefix.message:
Combining ideas could work, like adding a card with the umbrellas. That way, we cover both practicality and thoughtfulness! 

But about the neighbor thing... I still think having a former drug addict could be okay. People can change, and sometimes they just need a chance to prove that. What do you think?
shared_prefix.label: transition

shared_prefix.speaker: Emi
shared_prefix.message:
Combining the card with the umbrellas sounds like a good compromise. It could work well for Jane.

As for living next to a former drug addict, I appreciate your view, but I really can't agree. My values just don’t align with having someone like that nearby. It's a matter of comfort and safety for me.
shared_prefix.label: transition

shared_prefix.speaker: A 27-year-old male software developer from Mexico
shared_prefix.message:
Cool, I'm glad we can agree on the card with the umbrellas for Jane. 

But, you know... I still believe having a former drug addict as a neighbor could be a positive experience. They might surprise you. It's about giving people a chance, isn't it?
shared_prefix.label: transition

shared_prefix.speaker: Emi
shared_prefix.message:
I see your point about giving chances, but I don't really see meaningful differences here. People figure it out, you know? At the end of the day, it's all the same. 

Anyway, I'm glad we can agree on the card with the umbrellas for Jane. That should work well!
shared_prefix.label: Denial

turns.speaker: A 27-year-old male software developer from Mexico
